reason: Laser uranium enrichment (AVLIS, SILEX) was developed but is not commercial, so 'is used for uranium enrichment' overclaims.

fix.summary: When isotope shifts exceed the Doppler width (narrowed with collimated beams), narrow-band lasers can selectively excite and then ionize or dissociate one isotope. It was developed for uranium enrichment (AVLIS on atomic vapour, SILEX-type molecular schemes on UF6), which is not yet commercial. It is used in resonance-ionization ion sources for radioactive beams and for enriching medical-isotope precursors such as 176Yb.

reason: Laser-side effects are among the limits, not 'the' limits; implosion asymmetry and hydrodynamic instabilities also limit gain.

fix.summary: Inertial confinement fusion uses lasers as the driver. NIF's 192 frequency-tripled (351 nm) Nd:glass beams heat a hohlraum whose X-rays implode a D–T capsule, and since December 2022 some shots have released more fusion energy than the laser energy delivered to the target. On the laser side, frequency-conversion efficiency, beam smoothing and laser–plasma instabilities constrain performance, together with implosion symmetry and hydrodynamic instabilities.

reason: It needs a breaks field, so it cannot be an identity. CMS reported evidence in 2019; the observation came from ATLAS in 2019.

fix.summary: The QED vacuum's Euler–Heisenberg four-photon coupling acts like an optical χ^(3) Kerr nonlinearity of the vacuum. It was first seen as light-by-light scattering γγ → γγ in ultra-peripheral Pb–Pb collisions, using the quasi-real photon clouds of the nuclei (ATLAS evidence 2017, CMS evidence 2019, ATLAS observation 2019). The related Breit–Wheeler process γγ → e+e− is also measured there.

reason: This is a specific, narrow method transfer; it is not structural in a graduate course of both fields.
BDMPS is the same coherent formation-time mechanism, made non-Abelian, so 'mechanism' fits. LPM is rarely taught in graduate EM, so strength 3 is inflated.
Photoabsorption and pair production are not light-scattering theory, and detection using these cross sections is a 'Y uses X' link.
The Rayleigh-like low-energy structure fails above pion threshold and at the Δ resonance, so this is not an identity in every regime.
It carries breaks (self-screening, λ_J, nonlinear dynamics), and the Fourier relation holds only for short junctions, so it is not an identity.
'Every LCD' is too strong: in-plane-switching and guest–host displays do not use the Fréedericksz transition between crossed polarizers.

fix.summary: A nematic is a uniaxial birefringent medium with its optic axis along the director. Jones-calculus retardation between crossed polarizers, switched by the field-driven Fréedericksz transition, is how twisted- and vertically-aligned nematic LCDs work. Cholesterics add selective Bragg reflection of one circular polarization, and q-plates with a patterned director imprint Pancharatnam–Berry phases.

reason: Measured binding energies are about 0.2–0.5 eV depending on the surroundings. Graduate EM does not teach Keldysh screening, so strength 3 is inflated.

fix.summary: Thin-film electrostatics of a polarizable sheet gives a potential that is logarithmic below the screening length r0 and 1/r beyond it. This explains the non-hydrogenic Rydberg series and the exciton binding energies of monolayer TMDs, about 0.2–0.5 eV depending on the dielectric surroundings. Changing those surroundings (encapsulation) shifts the gap and the binding energy, an approach called Coulomb engineering.

reason: Weiss mean-field theory is structural in condensed matter but not in electromagnetism, so strength 3 is inflated.
This describes a disputed phenomenon, not a method transfer. The record calls it contested, so the confidence must be 'proposed' and the disputants named.

fix.breaks: Dodge, van der Marel and co-workers argue that the transient optical signatures (notably in K3C60) can arise without superconductivity. Others attribute them to heating, inhomogeneity or reflectivity-modelling artefacts. The magnetic-expulsion reports are unreplicated.

reason: Coronagraphy is Fourier-plane spatial filtering, not van Cittert–Zernike. The summary is too vague: it names no technique-to-consequence map.

fix.summary: Direct imaging of exoplanets is Fourier-optics engineering. A Lyot coronagraph blocks the star in the focal plane and filters its diffracted light at the pupil-plane Lyot stop, and apodization and deformable mirrors dig a dark hole in the PSF. Bracewell nulling interferometry places a destructive fringe on the star. An Earth twin in visible light needs about 1e-10 contrast at a few λ/D.
fix.map: Focal-plane field = Fourier transform of the pupil field; star suppressed by a mask plus a pupil stop; required contrast ≈ 1e-10 at ~2–4 λ/D

reason: Strong-field lensing leaves the weak-field effective-index picture, not geometric optics. Wave effects appear only when λ is comparable to the Schwarzschild radius of the lens.

fix.breaks: The effective index holds only for weak, static fields. Gravitational lenses have no single focal point because the deflection is not linear in impact parameter, and the mass profile fixes the image configuration. Near the photon sphere the full null-geodesic equations are needed, and when λ ≳ R_s wave optics takes over.

reason: Trivial 'astronomy uses telescopes' link: it names no specific technique or consequence for transient science.
Interference between images is predicted, not yet observed. The map's normalization is wrong. Lensing diffraction is the same Fresnel–Kirchhoff physics, so this is not an analogy.

fix.summary: For wavelengths approaching the lens's Schwarzschild radius (gravitational waves from LIGO to LISA, coherent FRBs), lensing must be computed with the Fresnel–Kirchhoff diffraction integral over the lens plane, with the Fermat time delay as the phase. This gives frequency-dependent amplification and interference fringes between images. Searches are ongoing, with no confirmed detection.
fix.map: F(w)=(w/2πi)∫d²x exp[iwT(x)], w=4GM_z ω/c³; geometric optics recovered for w≫1
fix.breaks: Scalar thin-lens approximation; GW polarization and strong-field corrections are neglected.

reason: CMB polarimetry using Stokes parameters is a 'Y uses X' link, so strength 3 is inflated. The E/B description is imprecise.

fix.summary: CMB linear polarization is described with optical Stokes Q and U. On the sky they form a spin-2 field, which is expanded in spin-weighted harmonics and split into parity-even, gradient-like E modes and parity-odd, curl-like B modes. Primordial B modes would signal inflationary gravitational waves.

reason: It absorbs C1187. Strength 3 is inflated for a single-application link.

fix.summary: The cold-plasma index n²=1−ω_p²/ω² delays low frequencies (dispersion measure, Δt ≈ 4.15 ms·DM·ν_GHz^-2), and the magnetized plasma's circular birefringence rotates the polarization angle as RM·λ². DM versus redshift for localized FRBs counts intergalactic baryons (the Macquart relation), and RM measures the line-of-sight magnetic field. Turbulent density fluctuations add multipath scattering broadening.
fix.map: Δt ∝ DM ν^-2, DM=∫n_e dl; χ=χ0+RM λ², RM ∝ ∫n_e B_∥ dl

reason: duplicate of C1186. Scattering broadening comes from density turbulence, not from the dispersion relation.
MHD also requires Ohm's law; the summary omits it and the governing parameter, the magnetic Reynolds number.

fix.summary: Faraday's law, Ampère's law without displacement current and Ohm's law in a moving conductor combine into the induction equation. At the Sun's huge magnetic Reynolds numbers, field lines are frozen into the plasma (Alfvén's theorem). Flux emergence, sunspots and the dynamo follow, and flares release stored magnetic energy where thin current sheets break flux freezing (reconnection).
fix.breaks: The displacement current and charge separation are dropped (low-frequency, quasi-neutral limit). Fast reconnection requires non-ideal terms beyond resistive MHD (Hall, kinetic).

reason: Superluminal motion is a light-travel-time effect, not a field transformation. The boost exponent is 3+α only for discrete blobs. Beaming lives in radiation-from-moving-charges.

fix.summary: Relativistic aberration beams jet emission into a cone of half-angle ~1/Γ, and Doppler boosting multiplies the observed flux by δ^(3+α) for a discrete blob or δ^(2+α) for a continuous jet. This explains blazar dominance and one-sided jets. Apparent superluminal motion, β_app = β sinθ/(1−β cosθ), is the light-travel-time effect of the same kinematics.
fix.map: δ=1/[Γ(1−β cosθ)], S_ν ∝ δ^(3+α) (blob) or δ^(2+α) (jet), β_app=β sinθ/(1−β cosθ)

reason: Binary stars and stellar populations is a poor node. The strongest astrophysical use of masers is VLBI parallaxes of star-forming-region masers mapping the Galaxy.

fix.summary: Population inversion pumped by radiation or collisions makes OH, H2O and CH3OH masers in star-forming regions and evolved-star envelopes. They are single-pass amplifiers with exponential gain along velocity-coherent paths. Their compact, bright, narrow lines allow VLBI trigonometric parallaxes and proper motions that map the Milky Way's spiral arms and rotation curve.

reason: FRB emission is coherent and its mechanism is unknown, not incoherent synchrotron or IC. This is an emission mechanism, not a shared object.

fix.summary: Synchrotron, bremsstrahlung and inverse-Compton emission from relativistic charges, derived from Liénard–Wiechert fields, account for the broadband non-thermal spectra of AGN jets, GRB afterglows, pulsar wind nebulae and supernova remnants. The spectral indices map onto the power-law index of the electron distribution.

reason: It absorbs C1195. Neutrino telescopes using Cherenkov light is a 'Y uses X' link, so strength 3 is too high.

fix.summary: IceCube and KM3NeT detect Cherenkov light from the relativistic charged secondaries of neutrino interactions in ice and water. The cos θ = 1/(nβ) cone and photon arrival times give the direction. The Frank–Tamm yield, together with the dispersion, absorption and scattering of the medium, sets the light output and energy scale. At the highest energies, Askaryan radio Cherenkov emission is used.

reason: duplicate of C1194
Vacuum-dipole spin-down needs breaks: magnetospheres are plasma-filled and measured braking indices are mostly below 3. It is not an identity.

fix.summary: Treating a pulsar as a rotating magnetic dipole gives a spin-down power ∝ B²R⁶Ω⁴. This yields the braking index n=3, the characteristic age P/2Ṗ and the standard surface-field estimates from P and Ṗ.
fix.breaks: Real magnetospheres are plasma-filled: force-free solutions (Spitkovsky 2006) give L ∝ (1+sin²α), so even aligned rotators spin down. Measured braking indices are mostly below 3.

reason: Electromagnetism does not study AGN jets; synchrotron is the emission mechanism, not a shared object.
The map formula is dimensionally wrong (μ0 belongs in the denominator) and the braking part duplicates C1196. Pulsar emission mechanisms are not settled.

fix.summary: Charges accelerated along curved open field lines in pulsar magnetospheres emit curvature radiation, whose spectrum is the synchrotron one with the field-line radius of curvature in place of the gyroradius. This, plus synchrotron emission from secondary pairs, is the leading model for GeV pulses. The coherent radio emission mechanism remains unresolved.

reason: This is an emission mechanism, not a shared object. The summary should name the X-ray rim diagnostic.

fix.summary: Radio and X-ray synchrotron emission from electrons accelerated at remnant shocks reveals diffusive shock acceleration up to ~100 TeV (SN 1006). The narrow X-ray rims, limited by synchrotron cooling lengths, show magnetic fields amplified to ~100 μG, which links to the origin of Galactic cosmic rays.

reason: Thomson scattering produces net linear polarization only from a quadrupole anisotropy of the incident radiation, not from anisotropy in general.

fix.summary: Thomson scattering by free electrons of radiation with a local quadrupole anisotropy generates linear polarization, because of the |ε·ε'|² angular dependence. In the CMB this produces E modes at recombination and the large-angle reionization bump, and only tensor perturbations or lensing produce B modes.

reason: The GRB compactness bound on Γ comes from γγ→e+e− pair opacity, not the Thomson optical depth.

fix.summary: The Thomson optical depth of the outflow sets the photospheric radius and any quasi-thermal photospheric component of GRB prompt emission. Inverse-Compton scattering adds GeV–TeV afterglow components (synchrotron self-Compton, seen by MAGIC and H.E.S.S.). The compactness bound on the Lorentz factor comes from avoiding γγ pair-production opacity.
fix.map: τ_T = n_e σ_T R/Γ (comoving); Γ_min from τ_γγ(E_max) < 1

reason: This is a 'Y uses X' link, so strength 3 is inflated. The specific consequence is the slope-to-scale-height relation.

fix.summary: Rayleigh scattering by H2 or small haze particles makes the apparent planet radius grow toward the blue, and the slope measures the atmospheric scale height. Mie-regime clouds and hazes flatten transmission spectra and mute molecular features.
fix.map: dR_p/d ln λ = −4H for σ ∝ λ^-4, H = k_BT/μg

reason: Phase plates create speckle rather than reduce it. Temporal and polarization smoothing make the speckle move faster than instabilities grow.

fix.summary: Random or continuous phase plates fix the far-field envelope but impose a fully developed speckle pattern of λf/D-sized hot spots. Induced spatial incoherence, smoothing by spectral dispersion and polarization smoothing reduce the coherence time, so the speckles move faster than filamentation and parametric instabilities can grow. This lowers laser imprint and backscatter in ICF.
fix.map: speckle width ≈ λ f/D, speckle length ≈ 7λ(f/D)²; coherence time ≈ 1/Δν < instability growth time

record.name: Incoherent Thomson scattering diagnostic of T_e and n_e
record.summary: Laser light Thomson-scattered by plasma electrons (scattering parameter α=1/kλ_D≪1) is Doppler-broadened by their thermal motion. The spectral width gives T_e and the absolute scattered power gives n_e, making Thomson scattering the reference profile diagnostic on tokamaks.

record.name: Electron-cyclotron emission radiometry of T_e profiles
record.summary: Gyrating electrons radiate at harmonics of ω_ce = eB/m_e. Because B ∝ 1/R in a tokamak, each frequency maps to a major radius, and the optically thick second harmonic radiates as a blackbody (Rayleigh–Jeans). ECE radiometers therefore give time-resolved T_e(R) profiles.

record.name: Waveguide cutoff and plasma cutoff share ω²=ω_c²+c²k²
record.summary: A waveguide mode and a transverse wave in an unmagnetized plasma obey the same Klein–Gordon dispersion: below ω_c (waveguide) or ω_p (plasma) the wave is evanescent. Above it, v_ph v_g = c², so the group velocity is less than c in both.
record.map: ω² = ω_mn² + c²k² ↔ ω² = ω_p² + c²k²
record.breaks: The waveguide cutoff comes from transverse confinement, whereas the plasma cutoff comes from collective electron inertia. Plasma adds thermal and magnetic corrections, Landau damping and longitudinal Langmuir modes, none of which a waveguide has.

record.name: Ponderomotive potential: HHG cutoff and laser wakefields
record.summary: The cycle-averaged quiver energy U_p sets the 3.17U_p HHG cutoff for a single electron. In a plasma its gradient is the ponderomotive force, which expels electrons to drive laser wakefield acceleration (Tajima–Dawson) and relativistic self-focusing once a0 ≳ 1.
